nl: A resistance–load reliability problem. The resistance R follows a normal distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 12. The load effect S follows a normal distribution with mean 40 and standard deviation 8. R and S are independent. Failure occurs when the load effect exceeds the resistance (limit state g = R − S).

A steel beam in bending. The yield strength Fy (MPa) is lognormal with mean 350 and standard deviation 25. The section modulus Z (cm³) is normal with mean 500 and standard deviation 10. The applied moment M (kN·m) follows a Gumbel (extreme-value) distribution with mean 120 and standard deviation 30. The three variables are independent. The yield moment capacity is Fy·Z/1000 (kN·m), and failure occurs when the applied moment exceeds this capacity (limit state g = Fy·Z/1000 − M).

A short concrete column under axial compression. The compressive strength fc (MPa) is lognormal with mean 32 and standard deviation 5. The applied stress σ (MPa) is lognormal with mean 10 and standard deviation 2.2. The two variables are independent. Failure occurs when the applied stress exceeds the compressive strength (limit state g = fc − σ).

A slender column checked against Euler buckling. The elastic modulus E (MPa) is lognormal with mean 200000 and standard deviation 10000. The second moment of area I (m⁴) is lognormal with mean 8.33×10⁻⁶ and standard deviation 4×10⁻⁷. The column length L (m) is normal with mean 3.0 and standard deviation 0.03. The axial load P (kN) follows a Gumbel distribution with mean 1000 and standard deviation 200. All variables are independent. Failure occurs when the axial load exceeds the Euler critical buckling load (limit state g = π²·E·1000·I/L² − P).

A nonlinear reliability problem with a strongly curved limit-state surface. Two independent variables X1 and X2 are each normally distributed with mean 1.0 and standard deviation 0.2. The limit state is g = exp(X1/X2) − 1.5, with failure when g < 0.

A highly nonlinear reliability problem whose failure surface is curved by a sinusoidal term. Two independent variables are normally distributed: X1 (a phase variable) with mean 1.5 and standard deviation 0.3, and X2 (an amplitude) with mean 2.0 and standard deviation 0.4. The limit state is g = sin(X1)·X2 − 0.5, with failure when g < 0.

A fatigue check under an S-N power law. The fatigue limit Sf (MPa) is lognormal with mean 100 and standard deviation 15. The applied stress range Sa (MPa) follows a Weibull distribution with mean 50 and standard deviation 15. The two variables are independent. The accumulated damage is (Sa/Sf)⁴, and failure occurs when this damage reaches 1 (limit state g = 1 − (Sa/Sf)⁴).

A nuclear containment pressure check. The containment pressure capacity Pcap (kPa) is lognormal with mean 500 and standard deviation 30. The internal pressure demand Pdem (kPa) follows a Gumbel distribution with mean 220 and standard deviation 36. The two variables are independent. Failure occurs when the internal pressure demand exceeds the containment capacity (limit state g = Pcap − Pdem).

A pile group in which the weakest of three piles governs failure (a series system). Each pile's undrained strength cu1, cu2, cu3 (kPa) is lognormal with mean 60 and standard deviation 15, and the three strengths are mutually correlated with a correlation coefficient of 0.5. The shared axial load Q (kN) follows a Gumbel distribution with mean 120 and standard deviation 30 and is independent of the strengths; each pile carries one third of it. Failure occurs when the weakest pile capacity falls below the load per pile (limit state g = min(cu1, cu2, cu3) − Q/3).

An offshore jacket structure with ten independent random variables. Five member capacities R1–R5 are each lognormal with mean 1000 and standard deviation 150. Five environmental load contributions S1–S5 are each Gumbel-distributed with mean 500 and standard deviation 100. Failure occurs when the total load exceeds the total capacity (limit state g = (R1+R2+R3+R4+R5) − (S1+S2+S3+S4+S5)).

A quality-control problem. The quality factor X is Beta-distributed on the interval [0, 1] with mean 0.65 and standard deviation 0.08. The stress-utilization noise Y is normal with mean 0.1 and standard deviation 0.03. The two variables are independent. Failure occurs when the quality factor falls below a threshold of 0.35 plus the noise (limit state g = X − 0.35 − Y).

A slope-stability problem. The friction angle φ (degrees) is normal with mean 32 and standard deviation 3. The cohesion c (kPa) is lognormal with mean 22 and standard deviation 4. The driving normal stress σ (kPa) follows a Gumbel distribution with mean 22 and standard deviation 5. All three variables are independent, and φ is used in degrees (converted to radians inside the trigonometric functions). Failure occurs when the driving stress exceeds the resisting stress, given by the nonlinear limit state g = c·cos(φ) + σ·tan(φ)·√(1 + 0.05·(φ − 32)²) − σ.

A vibration serviceability check with a two-sided acceptance band. The response V is chi-square distributed with mean 6.0 and standard deviation 3.464 (six degrees of freedom). The half-width capacity C is normal with mean 4.0 and standard deviation 0.6. The two variables are independent. The response must stay within C of the nominal value 6.0; deviating in either direction fails the check (limit state g = C − |V − 6.0|).

A structure under extreme wind loading. The wind resistance R (kN) is lognormal with mean 800 and standard deviation 80. The extreme wind load W (kN) follows a Fréchet (Extreme-Value Type II) distribution with mean 400 and standard deviation 120. The two variables are independent. Failure occurs when the extreme wind load exceeds the resistance (limit state g = R − W).

A sea-wall overtopping problem. The significant wave height H (m) follows a Rayleigh distribution with mean 2.5 and standard deviation 1.31. The deck elevation D (m) is normal with mean 7.0 and standard deviation 0.3. The two variables are independent. Overtopping (failure) occurs when 1.2 times the wave height exceeds the deck elevation (limit state g = D − 1.2·H).

A highway bridge girder. The yield strength Fy (MPa) is lognormal with mean 350 and standard deviation 20, and the section modulus Z (cm³) is normal with mean 600 and standard deviation 10; both are independent. The three live-load moments M1, M2, M3 (one per lane) each follow a Gumbel distribution with mean 50 and standard deviation 10, and they share a traffic correlation of 0.4 with one another. The moment capacity is Fy·Z/1000, and failure occurs when the total live-load moment exceeds it (limit state g = Fy·Z/1000 − (M1 + M2 + M3)).

A thirty-dimensional parallel redundant system with all variables independent. There are fifteen resistance terms R01 through R15, each lognormal with mean 100 and standard deviation 20, and fifteen load terms S01 through S15, each normal with mean 75 and standard deviation 10. Failure occurs when the sum of the load terms exceeds the sum of the resistance terms (limit state g = (R01 + R02 + … + R15) − (S01 + S02 + … + S15)).

A minimum yield-strength problem. The minimum yield strength Fmin (MPa) across specimens follows a Type-I Smallest (Gumbel-minimum) extreme-value distribution with mean 280 and standard deviation 25. The applied demand D (MPa) is lognormal with mean 180 and standard deviation 30. The two variables are independent. Failure occurs when the applied demand exceeds the minimum yield strength (limit state g = Fmin − D).

A minimum-strength problem with a mechanical lower threshold. The minimum capacity Rmin follows a Type-III Smallest (Weibull-minimum) distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 15, shifted by a threshold ε = 50 below which the strength cannot fall. The applied load L is normal with mean 70 and standard deviation 10. The two variables are independent. Failure occurs when the applied load exceeds the minimum capacity (limit state g = Rmin − L).

A corrosion-degradation problem. The component lifetime T (years) is exponentially distributed with mean 50 and standard deviation 50. The inspection age Tins (years) is lognormal with mean 1.0 and standard deviation 0.2. The two variables are independent. Failure occurs when the lifetime is shorter than the inspection age (limit state g = T − Tins).
